summary: Zero depth. Colour and type do all the work, and every state is carried by fill.
source: Tilda Flat + cheat sheet · Looka §10 · dev.to · NN/g 'Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users' · Microsoft Metro 2010 / iOS 7 2013 / Material 2014

surface.role: panels sit on the ground with no elevation

blue.role: primary fill. Carries white at 14px (6.3:1). This is the base.

bluePressed.role: the pressed step (9.0:1 with white). The whole interaction system is these two.

blueTint.role: NON-TEXT only — borders, chart fills, decorative areas. 4.33:1 with white, which fails body text.

sand.role: a warm neutral block. Takes ink text

amberLight.role: the hero band fill. Carries INK at 5.6:1 — #b9770e is only 2.99:1 with ink and fails even the 3:1 large-text floor

radius.note: 0, or ONE small consistent value. Never mixed.

shadow.rule: box-shadow of any kind is banned — that is Material, not flat

focus.reason: flat gave up depth, so it cannot use a shadow ring. Ink on any pack fill clears 3:1, and a 3px ring is thick enough to read without elevation.

motion.note: STATE IS CARRIED BY FILL. Define a two-step ramp for every interactive colour: base and pressed. That is the entire interaction system.

copyBudget.headlineReason: flat headings are bold and large; seven words is the practical ceiling

a11y.signifierWarning: NN/g: flat design's missing depth cues have been 'reducing user efficiency by complicating users' understanding of what's clickable'. This pack gave up two of the three clickability channels, so the resting state MUST identify controls through type, colour, contrast and wording. Hover may stay supplemental (WCAG 1.4.11 exempts it) but rest may not.
a11y.contrastNote: The canonical flat palette fails AA on white. #3498db is 2.9:1 and #2ecc71 is 1.9:1. This pack darkens every hue until it clears 4.5:1 — that is not a deviation from flat, it is flat done correctly.
a11y.secondaryNote: Outline buttons must use the PRESSED step for their text and border, not the base. The base primary is tuned for white-on-fill; as ink-on-ground it is 3.77:1 and fails.
a11y.flatBlueNote: The canonical flat blue #3498db is 2.9:1 on white and unusable for text. Darkening to #2f7fb8 gives 4.33:1 with white — which clears LARGE text (3:1) but still fails 14px body (4.5:1). Every fill that sits under white body text therefore uses #20628f (6.3:1), and #2f7fb8 is demoted to a non-text tint. THIS IS THE FINDING: a flat palette has to be re-derived against the text sizes it will carry, not darkened until one sample passes. The self-audit surfaced it four separate times — nav pill, hero band, secondary button, primary button — before the ramp itself was corrected.
a11y.paletteNote: Flat is the one pack in the catalogue with a deliberately WIDE palette. Tilda and the reference galleries show 5-8 hue compositions as the norm, not the exception. The constraint is not hue COUNT, it is that every hue is a flat fill with no gradient and no depth, and that any hue carrying text is derived against that text size.
a11y.onColorNote: Outline/ghost controls inherit a colour derived against the page ground. On a coloured band that derivation is invalid — the flat secondary is 2.59:1 on the amber hero. Controls on a coloured band must take the same ink-or-white the band's own text uses.
a11y.amberNote: #b9770e was chosen to carry WHITE text (4.6:1) but the hero band carries INK, where it is only 2.99:1 — under even the 3:1 large-text floor. A hue tuned for one text colour is not tuned for the other; the band uses #e8a33d (5.6:1 with ink) instead. Same lesson as the blue ramp, from the opposite direction.

banned: depth-based elevation systems — that is Material, not flat

darkMode.note: Ground goes #1b2631, surface #22303c. The hues LIGHTEN rather than darken — #2f7fb8 on a dark ground is 3.4:1 and fails body text, so it moves to #5dade2 (6.1:1). A flat palette must be re-derived per theme, not inverted.

scroll.headline: scroll-theme-shift (●)
scroll.reason: the standout for this pack: solid colour swaps with no gradients are exactly what flat is made of, and a theme shift costs nothing to composite.
banned: parallax — the style bans depth, and parallax IS depth. There is no conditional form
video-scrub — the heaviest possible payload, in the style whose pitch is lightness
scroll.legibilityRule: A theme shift interpolates the background across the whole scroll range, so the text must clear contrast at BOTH ends and everywhere between. Shifting from the light page ground to the primary left white text at 1.15:1 for the first half. Shift ink -> primary instead: white is 11.6:1 at the start and 4.6:1 at the end.

sheet.metaLine: no shadow · no gradient · 4px radius · two-step colour ramp
tokenTable: base and pressed — both carry white body text
NON-TEXT only. 4.33:1 with white — fails body copy

notes.tokens: Because there is no depth, state must be carried by fill. Every interactive colour needs a two-step ramp — base and pressed — derived against the text size it will carry. #2f7fb8 looks like a fine flat blue and clears large text at 4.33:1, but fails 14px body; it is demoted here to a non-text tint. And note the palette is wide on purpose: flat is the one pack here that runs 5–8 hues.
notes.nav: A solid bar in the ink colour. No shadow under it, no border — the colour change alone separates it from the ground. This is flat's honest version of elevation.
notes.hero: Large bold type on a flat fill. The whole hero is one rectangle of colour; there is no card, no shadow and no layering, so hierarchy comes entirely from size and fill.
notes.button: NN/g's finding lands right here. Flat gave up two of the three clickability channels, so the resting state has to identify the control through fill and weight. Hover darkens one step; there is nothing else available.
notes.form: A field is a white box with a 2px border — the border IS the affordance, since there is no inset shadow to sink it. Error swaps the border to red AND adds text, because colour alone fails 1.4.1.
notes.card: A white rectangle on the grey ground. No shadow, no border needed — the surface/ground contrast does the separating. This is the one thing flat does more cleanly than any other pack.
notes.table: Zebra striping is legitimate here and nowhere else in the catalogue: with no rules and no shadows, an alternating fill is the only separation available that is not a border.
notes.overlay: A flat scrim and a flat panel. The dialog is distinguished by fill alone — which is exactly the limitation NN/g describes, and why the primary action carries the strongest colour on the page.
notes.empty: A 2px dashed border in the muted ink. Flat has no shadow to remove and no material to omit, so absence has to be drawn.
notes.dark: A flat palette must be re-derived per theme, not inverted. #2f7fb8 is 3.4:1 on a dark ground and fails body text; it moves to #5dade2 at 6.1:1. Inverting a flat palette is the commonest way this style ships broken in dark mode.
notes.narrow: Flat is the most robust pack at narrow width — no shadows to clip, no grid to collapse, no depth to lose. Only the gap and the type scale change.
notes.copy: Keeps the engine's 420. Flat has no legibility tax to pay.
